notes: The feed registry as data: which multicast group carries which feed, on which ports, with which
published set of channels. That allocation is the publisher's to decide and it changes without our
involvement, which is why it is a document and not code.
SUPPLY. --feed-registry-url, then --feed-registry <path>, else the copy compiled into the binary.
The compiled copy is a last-known-good, so the container runs standalone and survives a fetch that
fails. Resolution happens once at startup and there is no hot reload; the "feed registry resolved"
log line reports which document won, with its origin, version and row count.
ROWS. `code` is the group identifier `doublezero status --json` reports, and the reconciler
activates a row only while the host is subscribed to that code. `group` is the multicast address.
`kind` picks the protocol and with it the port roles: TopOfBook and Midpoint bind mktdata and
refdata, MarketByPrice and MarketByOrder add an in-band snapshot the book recovery depends on.
`emit_trades` is a capability claim, not a promise that this row prints the tape - where two rows
of one venue both claim it, which one prints is decided at runtime. `publishers` is either
`explicit`, one port block written out per publisher, or `derived`, a published set of channels
plus per-role bases that expands to base + channel_id, one publisher per channel.
SILENT FAILURES. A wrong value is never reported as one. Each layer fails differently:
- a `code` no live group matches -> the row never activates: no warning, no failed bind.
- a wrong mktdata port           -> no datagrams and dz_receiver_up 0. Visible.
- a wrong refdata port           -> reference data never resolves a definition, and every
processor gates emission on one, so the receiver reads
healthy and emits nothing.
- a wrong snapshot port          -> books stay Recovering forever, so that publisher contributes
no depth while still reading healthy.
The signal for the last two is dz_datagrams_received_total{role} pinned at 0.
SOURCES. `sources` is the optional Source ID -> name allocation. A name is emitted verbatim as
`venue`/`source_name` on the wire and as every `venue=` metric label, so it must be uppercase. An
id may appear only once; several ids may share a name (one venue running several matching
engines), and a row then says which id it carries with `source_id`, so each engine keeps its own
health and status. `source_id` must be an id this block assigns to the row's own `venue`. An id
this block does not assign is not an error: it gets a synthesized SOURCE_<id> label. Id 0 and the
SOURCE_<id>/UNREGISTERED names are reserved for that and refused here. A row's own `venue` is only
the default for Source IDs this document does not assign; the Source ID on the wire is
authoritative, and a publisher stamping one that is not its own is a publisher defect, corrected
at the publisher and never remapped here.
A binary older than the `sources` block ignores it and validates rows against its own built-in
table, so under a URL origin a row whose `venue` only this block resolves is rejected and the
WHOLE document degrades to that binary's built-in copy - losing every other change in the same
republish. Assign only names the deployed fleet already resolves.
EDITING. An unknown key is warned about by path and ignored, so an additive republish reaches an
older fleet without a rebuild; a missing required field stays fatal, so a typo cannot quietly
default. `version` bumps only for a change that reinterprets what an existing field MEANS - adding
one is not a bump.

Phoenix perpetuals, top of book and trades. Depth for the same venue is the market-by-price row
below, on its own group.
CHANNELS. One, id 1, on both roles (schema v3). It must agree with the market-by-price sibling's
refdata channel: the instrument catalog is keyed on the refdata channel, so a divergence lists
every Phoenix product twice and makes the bare PHOENIX:SYMBOL product ids ambiguous.
PUBLISHERS. Three, all on these ports and channel 1 with no mirror offset, told apart by source IP address.
TAPE. Both Phoenix rows claim it; the market-by-price row states how the two resolve.
Phoenix perpetuals, market-by-price depth, on its own group. The same publisher process as
edge-phoenix-tob, so the same manifest, the same instrument ids and the same schema v3.
CHANNELS. One, id 1, on all three roles - the channel the top-of-book row carries, for the reason
stated there.
PUBLISHERS. Three, all on these ports and channel 1 with no mirror offset, told apart by source IP address.
TAPE. Both rows claim it: this row's mktdata role carries Trade byte-identical to the top-of-book
row's. The reconciler ranks TopOfBook above MarketByPrice when both run, and the overlap at a
handover collapses in the trade_id dedup window, which depends on Phoenix stamping its real venue
trade ids. Were it to stamp the zero sentinel instead, a handover would double-print, and
silently: the guard that would catch it keys its owner on the source IP address, and these two
rows are one process behind one address, so dz_trades_no_id_conflict_total cannot fire for them. A
consumer's own fill count is the only tripwire.
